issues.legal_issue: A Magistrate may direct further investigation after a police report has been filed and cognizance has been taken, until the trial commences, including after process has issued and the accused has appeared.
material_facts: The police filed a charge-sheet, the Magistrate took cognizance and issued summons, and the accused appeared.
The accused applied for further investigation after cognizance had been taken.
The investigation and inquiry had not reached commencement of trial, which occurs when the relevant charges are framed or, in a summons case, when the accused is asked to plead or state a defence.
issues.conclusion: The Magistrate retains power to direct further investigation after a police report and cognizance, including after process has issued and the accused has appeared, up to commencement of trial. The power may be exercised suo motu or on an application, but does not extend to ordering a fresh or de novo investigation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 156(1), 156(3), 173(8), and 2(h) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, read with Article 21, permit the Magistrate to ensure a fair and proper investigation through further investigation until trial begins. Sections 190, 200, 202, and 204 form part of the procedural scheme. The Court relied on Sakiri Vasu v. State of U.P., State of Bihar v. J.A.C. Saldhana, Bhagwant Singh v. Commissioner of Police, Ram Lal Narang v. State (Delhi Administration), Union Public Service Commission v. S. Papaiah, Hasanbhai Valibhai Qureshi v. State of Gujarat, Hemant Dhasmana v. CBI, Samaj Parivartan Samudaya v. State of Karnataka, Vinay Tyagi v. Irshad Ali, and Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab. It rejected the contrary approach in Devarapalli Lakshminarayana Reddy and overruled, to the extent inconsistent, Amrutbhai Shambubhai Patel, Athul Rao, Bikash Ranjan Rout, Randhir Singh Rana, and Reeta Nag.

rule.if: criminal_case_on_police_report and post_report_proceeding and before_trial_commences and further_evidence_needed_for_fair_investigation

predicates.criminal_case_on_police_report: The criminal proceeding began with a police investigation and report to a Magistrate.
predicates.post_report_proceeding: The police report has been filed and the proceeding has continued before the Magistrate.
predicates.before_trial_commences: The relevant trial has not begun, including because charges have not been framed where charges are required.
predicates.further_evidence_needed_for_fair_investi: The circumstances indicate that collecting additional evidence is needed to achieve a fair and proper investigation.

issues.definition: When a police-report criminal proceeding remains before trial and additional evidence is needed for a fair investigation, the Magistrate may direct further investigation.

issues.legal_issue: Further investigation of an existing offence is not justified where the material sought to be investigated has no direct bearing on that offence and instead raises a separate alleged crime.
material_facts: The existing FIR alleged extortion and the creation or use of false documents concerning agricultural land.
The accused sought further investigation into allegations about the validity of land revenue entries and the complainants’ claim to the land.
The Court found those allegations had no direct bearing on the investigation of the existing FIR and were in the nature of allegations requiring a separate FIR.
The Sessions Judge had ordered further investigation into the existing FIR, and the High Court had set that order and resulting interim reports aside.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the setting aside of the order for further investigation into the existing FIR and the consequential interim reports because the requested inquiries concerned facts without a direct bearing on that FIR.
issues.legal_principle: Further investigation under Sections 156(3) and 173(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure concerns the offence under investigation and must serve a fair investigation of that matter. The Court applied the distinction between further investigation and a separate investigation, consistently with the principles in Vinay Tyagi v. Irshad Ali and the other authorities on further investigation; the facts sought to be investigated here called for a separate FIR rather than expansion of the existing investigation.

predicates.appeal_concerning_further_investigation: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an order for further investigation of an existing criminal case.
predicates.existing_police_report_case: A police report has already been filed in the criminal case under consideration.
predicates.requested_facts_unrelated_to_reported_of: The facts proposed for investigation concern alleged conduct that has no direct bearing on the offence reported in the existing case.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning further investigation, unrelated allegations do not justify further investigation of the offence in the existing police-report case.

issues.legal_issue: A court may direct the police to register a separate FIR where material before it presents serious allegations of a distinct criminal offence requiring investigation.
material_facts: An official communication described suspected forged documents and orders, applications made in the names of deceased persons, and possible fraud concerning the land.
The communication called for a thorough inquiry and criminal proceedings if warranted.
The Court found that these allegations did not call for further investigation into the existing FIR but required a separate police investigation.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the police to register an FIR based on the official communication and directed that a senior police officer investigate it and submit a report.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the need to secure justice by bringing serious alleged criminal conduct to the attention of the police for investigation. It distinguished a separate investigation into those allegations from further investigation under Sections 156(3) and 173(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure into the existing FIR.

predicates.appeal_reviewing_criminal_investigation_: The court is deciding an appeal involving the handling of criminal investigations.
predicates.official_communication_contains_serious_: An official communication describes serious alleged criminal conduct distinct from the offence under investigation in the existing case.
predicates.allegations_require_police_inquiry: The described allegations require investigation by the police to clarify whether an offence has occurred.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning criminal investigations reveals serious allegations of a distinct offence in an official communication that require police inquiry, the police must register a separate FIR.

issues.legal_issue: A court may defer commencement of an existing criminal trial until a police report is submitted in a newly directed investigation arising from related allegations.
material_facts: The Court directed registration and investigation of a separate FIR based on the official communication.
A trial in the existing FIR had been stayed pending the Court’s decision.

The Court directed that the existing trial not commence until the police report in the newly directed FIR was submitted, after which the Magistrate could consider whether the cases should be tried jointly or separately.
issues.conclusion: The existing trial was not to commence until the police report in the newly directed FIR had been submitted; the Magistrate was to decide thereafter whether to hold a joint trial or separate trials.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made this direction to coordinate the proceedings and allow the Magistrate to consider the relationship between the cases after the separate investigation report was available. It did not prescribe a general statutory rule for joint or separate trials.

predicates.court_directs_investigation_of_related_s: The court orders a separate police investigation into allegations related to an existing criminal proceeding.
predicates.existing_trial_is_pending: A trial in the existing criminal case has not yet commenced.
predicates.new_police_report_not_yet_submitted: The police have not yet submitted a report on the newly directed investigation.

issues.definition: When a related separate investigation has been ordered and its report is outstanding, the pending existing trial must wait for that report.
